notes:
Reading comics aloud: the app can finally see the text properly.

Words were coming out with letters missing — "SUICIDE" read as "sucde", "STRESS" as "stres" — and most of a page's text was never found at all, so a whole chapter would be spoken in a handful of lines and skip past in a few jumps.

One cause behind both. A webtoon chapter is a single enormous image, sometimes ten thousand pixels tall, and the text reader shrinks whatever it is given before it looks at it. A strip that tall arrived as a thumbnail with the lettering a few pixels high — the app was never really being shown the page, only a picture of it.

Tall pages are now read in slices, each at its true size, so the lettering is the size it was drawn. The slices overlap so a speech balloon sitting on a join is complete in at least one of them, and the repeats that creates are merged.

Also new, for anyone reporting a problem: turn on Settings > Narration timing and the caption strip gains a small line showing which voice engine actually spoke, which narrator, and what the app decided the line was. A screen recording then carries the answer to "which voice was that?" instead of leaving it to guesswork.
